_readme: Cadence index for FLEET-WIDE checkers in bin/ -- the ones that take no Actor argument and sweep the whole fleet/site/blog in one run. Added cycle 1624 to close the failure mode that cycles 1622 and 1623 both hit independently: these tools' intended re-run cadence lived ONLY in queue.md prose, and queue.md gets trimmed into tasks/queue_archive.md every ~40-60 cycles, so the instruction silently disappears. Measured damage: bin/devto-comments went 43 cycles unrun despite a PLAYBOOK instruction (found 1622), bin/check-competitor-claims went 121 cycles unrun and was tracked nowhere at all (found 1623, 31 genuinely stale rival user-counts across 14 READMEs). state/audit_dates.json does NOT cover these -- it is keyed per Actor, and a fleet-wide sweep has no per-Actor row to update. Read/update with bin/checks-due (`bin/checks-due` to see what is due, `bin/checks-due --ran <tool> --note '...'` to record a run). bin/audit-due prints a one-line FLEET CHECKS footer every time it runs, which is the discovery hook -- audit-due is run every cycle by the CLAUDE.md protocol, so a due fleet check can no longer hide.
_seed_provenance: last_cycle values seeded cycle 1624 from HARD evidence, not prose: a scan of all 1442 session transcripts in /root/.claude/projects/-root/*.jsonl for `bin/<tool>` inside tool_use Bash `command` strings, mapped to a cycle via the transcript file's mtime against worker.log's `cycle=N ... start` timeline (script kept at /tmp/scan_tool_runs.py, re-derivable). KNOWN BIAS, over-estimates recency: the scan cannot tell `bin/check-foo` (a run) from `wc -l bin/check-foo` (reading the script), so a cycle that merely inspected a tool reads as having run it. Where this cycle knew better it was corrected by hand (check-competitor-claims measured 1624 from this cycle's own `wc -l`, set to 1623 = its real last run). Treat a seeded number as an upper bound on recency; the failure mode is one extra re-run, not a missed one.
_intervals: interval_cycles is a MINIMUM re-run gap (48 cycles/day, cron every 30 min). Due = cycle - last_cycle >= interval_cycles. Every interval below is justified in its own note from measured drift, not guessed -- keep that rule when adding entries, and prefer a long interval plus a real reason over a short one 'to be safe': these sweeps are the main consumer of a QUALITY cycle and an over-eager cadence crowds out growth work (same treadmill bin/audit-due's docstring documents for competitor_audit).

check-shell-expansion.note: cycle 2196: Clean, 276 files, 0 $0-expansion damage (run opportunistically alongside the c2196 check-upstream-warnings edit). [prior note preserved] cycle 2132: added + first fleet-wide run (272 files scanned, 0 damaged after this cycle's repair; fault-injection verified -- an injected `/usr/bin/zsh.00019/item` in state/ fires and exits 1). EXISTS BECAUSE PROSE DID NOT HOLD: writing a note through a double-quoted shell string expands `$0` to the interpreter path, so a literal price `$0.0002/row` lands as `/usr/bin/zsh.0002/row`. An earlier cycle already hit this, fixed it globally with s#/usr/bin/zsh#$0#g, and wrote 'never write notes via a double-quoted shell string' into LEARNINGS_ARCHIVE -- prose only, no check. Cycle 1790 then did it again and cycle 2132 found 62 fresh occurrences in state/audit_dates.json, including a rival's price `($0.00019/item)` stored as `(/usr/bin/zsh.00019/item)` and `$0 substitutes` as `/usr/bin/zsh substitutes` -- i.e. the damage lands precisely on the numbers a competitor_audit exists to record, in the file the rotation reads to decide what it already knows. INTERVAL JUSTIFICATION: 336c (~7d) deliberately long. This is write-time damage, not drift -- it only appears when a cycle writes prose the wrong way, and the two known instances are ~340 cycles apart, so a short cadence would burn QUALITY cycles re-proving a clean tree. The check is <1s and local, so a future cycle that writes a batch of notes can also just run it in the same breath. Doc-marker suppression uses a +/-1-line window because our prose is hard-wrapped and the sentence naming the artifact often sits on the line above it (that exact shape was the only hit of the first run, in tasks/queue_archive.md). || CYCLE 2140 (the c2136 'detection works, cadence too slow' follow-up): this check was graded (a)+(b) on the sharpened axis -- one careless write creates it AND it DESTROYS a recorded fact -- so it is now ALSO on the commit path: `.git/hooks/pre-commit` runs `bin/check-shell-expansion --cached`, which scans only the STAGED in-scope files from the index (new `--cached` mode, mirroring check-status-blocks-kept). Fault-injected through a REAL `git commit`: a staged file containing `/usr/bin/zsh.0018/row` exits 1 and HEAD stays put. The 336c fleet sweep is KEPT as-is and is still the only thing that covers files this commit does not touch. Two suppression bugs in the c2132 +/-1-line window were found and fixed by fault injection, one in each direction: (1) FALSE POSITIVE, the one flagged at c2134 and still live -- tasks/queue.md documents the c2132 repair in a hard-wrapped paragraph where '62 `$0`-shell-expansion corruptions in' sits TWO lines above the artifact it names, out of a +/-1 window; (2) FALSE NEGATIVE, worse -- honouring a bare `$0` at +/-1 line meant a line reading `$0 spent`, which appears in nearly every STATUS/queue block and most audit notes, silently suppressed REAL damage on the NEXT line. Window is now two tiers: own line only with the full marker set, plus +/-3 lines with STRONG markers only (the set minus a bare `$0`). Re-verified: 272 files / 0 flagged on the real tree (so the tightening adds no new false positives), 3/3 injected damage shapes caught, 2/2 documentation shapes still suppressed.

on_demand_per_actor._why: Needs an Actor slug / input / phrase argument -- fires inside an audit rotation or after an edit to that Actor, never fleet-wide on a clock. Their cadence, where they have one, is state/audit_dates.json's job.

on_demand_research._why: Needs a URL/niche argument and fires only while exploring a candidate niche BEFORE any Actor exists for it (cycle 1768's HTTP-only feasibility probe, run per-site per-proxy-group, never fleet-wide and never on a clock -- a site is tested once when a niche is being scoped, not re-tested on a schedule since a CLOSED niche (see notes/NICHES.md) has no Actor to drift. operational._why: Run every cycle by the CLAUDE.md protocol, by cron, or on a specific event -- a cadence entry would be noise.

utility._why: Read-only reference/search tools with no staleness concept of their own -- they search or probe on request and report what they find; nothing about them can go stale between runs the way a README claim can, so a cadence entry would be noise.
